topics.title: Housing
topics.intro: Follow approvals, completed homes and access to public housing.

questions.title: Are housing plans turning into homes?
questions.note: Planning approvals and HPD completions cover different projects and programs. Approvals are not homes built; affordable completions include preservation as well as new construction.

questions.title: Who is getting public housing?
questions.note: The total and homeless-applicant subset cover conventional NYCHA housing. Section 8 is a separate program.

topics.title: Homelessness
topics.intro: Read shelter demand, housing exits and returns together.

questions.title: How do shelter demand and housing exits compare?
questions.note: The shelter population is a daily average. Entries and housing exits are annual flows, not the same people tracked through a cohort. A housing exit requires at least 30 days out of shelter.

questions.title: Do people return after leaving shelter?
questions.note: These rates follow single adults placed in housing in the prior fiscal year for one year. Subsidized and unsubsidized groups are different populations; the gap does not establish a causal subsidy effect.

topics.title: Schools
topics.intro: Separate day-to-day attendance from persistent absence.

questions.title: Are students attending regularly?
questions.note: Attendance measures days present; chronic absence measures students attending less than 90% of the year. These measures exclude charter schools and use school years.

questions.title: Are Pre-K seats being used?
questions.note: Enrollment and vacant seats are June 30 snapshots for a school year. Fewer vacant seats alone cannot distinguish higher enrollment from a reduction in available seats.

topics.title: Child care
topics.intro: Look at access to vouchers and how quickly applications are decided.

questions.title: How many children receive voucher-supported care?
questions.note: Voucher enrollment is an average, not a count of all distinct children served during the year. Non-mandated low-income vouchers are one component of the total.

questions.title: How quickly are voucher applications decided?
questions.note: Timely eligibility determinations and enrollment measure different steps. A decision within 30 days is not necessarily an approval or an enrollment.

topics.title: Streets and pests
topics.intro: Distinguish complaints, work completed and conditions on the ground.

questions.title: Are pothole requests being handled promptly?
questions.note: Work orders can contain multiple potholes. The closure-time measure covers 311 requests and excludes proactive crew pickups, so the three series have different scopes.

questions.title: What do rat inspections tell us?
questions.note: Initial inspections and follow-up compliance inspections examine different populations. These percentages describe inspected properties, not the prevalence of rats across the whole city.

topics.title: Public safety
topics.intro: Keep reported crime, arrests and response times distinct.

questions.title: How are reported crimes and arrests moving?
questions.note: Arrests and reported crimes are separate events. One crime can lead to several arrests or none, and an arrest may relate to an earlier year. Their quotient is not a clearance rate.

questions.title: Which parts of police response are being measured?
questions.note: Both measures cover all crimes in progress. End-to-end response begins when the caller finishes dialing; dispatch-and-travel time starts when the dispatcher receives the assignment. They are not interchangeable.

sourceNotes.title: DHS on housing exits
sourceNotes.text: DHS attributes the decline in family housing placements to fewer unsubsidized placements. It attributes increases in subsidized placements primarily to CityFHEPS and also cites efforts to expedite placements. This is the agency’s explanation, not a causal finding established by these counts.

sourceNotes.title: DOT on pothole repairs
sourceNotes.text: DOT says proactive repair blitzes largely drove the increase in potholes repaired. Its 311 request-closure time excludes those proactive repairs. The chapter reports that closure time increased but remained below its target.

sourceNotes.title: Direction and target in the report
sourceNotes.text: The printed report says fewer unfilled Pre-K seats is the desired direction. Its FY2026 result is below its numeric target. Earlier Open Data direction metadata disagreed; the explorer uses the printed direction for FY2026.

sourceNotes.title: Library definition change
sourceNotes.text: The FY2026 six-day opening measure includes branches closed for long-term renovations. Comparisons across that definition change are not scored.

sourceNotes.title: DOB historical revisions
sourceNotes.text: The chapter documents revisions to earlier complaint figures. The explorer uses the revised printed history and retains differing Open Data values in the detail table.
